newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean oil product exports to surge in 1997.
newsitem.headline: South Korean oil product exports to surge in 1997.

text.p: South Korea is expected to see another surge in the growth of oil product exports in 1997 after it posted a 30-percent rise in 1996, industry sources said on Friday.
Expanding refinery capacity has prompted increasing amounts of product exports. But the surplus production is being absorbed by Asia's growing demand, they said.

"Exports are likely to grow more than 30 percent this year with the increased production from the refiners following the expansions," said an official in charge of oil exports at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.
George Goundry, an energy analyst at HG Asia, has a more moderate view and sees growth in 1997 of 15 to 20 percent.
"Exports volume will go up through the roof this year," Goundry said. "But after that it would flatten out."
South Korea shipped abroad 159.8 million barrels of petroleum products in 1996, up 30 percent from 122.8 million barrels a year before, the ministry said in a statement on 1996.
"Exports of heavier oil such as fuel oil, kerosene and diesel will rise significantly because of slower local demand as a result of tougher environmental rules," the ministry official said.
The ministry said growth in petroleum products output and slowdown in domestic demand were behind the rise.
The oil refiners produced 724.1 million barrels of petroleum products in 1996 against 643.4 million a year earlier -- a rise of more than 12 percent.
Consumption, on the other hand, rose 6.5 percent to 721 million barrels in 1996 from 677.2 million a year before. That compared with 9.0-percent growth in 1995.

Production ballooned with the start up of Hyundai Oil Refinery Co's new 200,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit last May, Yukong Ltd's 200,000 bpd unit last October and LG-Caltex Oil Corp's 220,000 bpd unit last December.
South Korea's government-licenced refining capacity now stands at 2.44 million bpd, up from 1.82 million bpd at end of 1995. No capacity increase is expected this year.
But despite the expansion of South Korea's refineries, analysts said Asia still needs to import oil products from other regions in order to satisfy demand.
The Hawaii-based East-west Centre, has forecast net products demand from Asia-Pacific of 1.776 million bpd in 1997.
It sees gasoline in surplus by 75,000 bpd, but a deficit in key products like kerosene amounting to 201,000 bpd, 403,000 bpd for diesel and 660,000 bpd for liquefied petroleum gas.
But South Korea's surplus refining capacity compared with domestic consumption could last for just a few years, analysts said.

In a presentation earlier this month to a Singapore conference, Young-Seok Moon, a director at the Korea Energy Economics Institute, said domestic demand would start outpacing domestic supply by 8,000 bpd by 2000.
However, the shortfall would grow to 444,000 bpd by 2006 even as refining capacity grows to 2.882 million bpd.
